{{Short description|Mathematical operation on Galois modules}}
{{More citations needed|date=December 2009}}
In [[number theory]] and [[algebraic geometry]], the '''Tate twist''',<ref>'The Tate Twist', in ''[[Lecture Notes in Mathematics]]'', Vol 1604, 1995, Springer, Berlin p.98–102</ref><ref>'The Tate Twist', https://ncatlab.org/nlab/show/Tate+twist </ref> named after [[John Tate (mathematician)|John Tate]], is an operation on [[Galois module]]s.

For example, if ''K'' is a [[field (mathematics)|field]], ''G<sub>K</sub>'' is its [[absolute Galois group]], and ρ : ''G<sub>K</sub>'' → Aut<sub>'''Q'''<sub>''p''</sub></sub>(''V'') is a [[group representation|representation]] of ''G<sub>K</sub>'' on a finite-dimensional [[vector space]] ''V'' over the field '''Q'''<sub>''p''</sub> of [[p-adic number|''p''-adic numbers]], then the Tate twist of ''V'', denoted ''V''(1), is the representation on the [[tensor product of representations|tensor product]] ''V''⊗'''Q'''<sub>''p''</sub>(1), where '''Q'''<sub>''p''</sub>(1) is the [[cyclotomic character|''p''-adic cyclotomic character]] (i.e. the [[Tate module]] of the group of [[roots of unity]] in the [[separable closure]] ''K<sup>s</sup>'' of ''K''). More generally, if ''m'' is a [[positive integer]], the '''''m''th Tate twist of ''V''''', denoted ''V''(''m''), is the tensor product of ''V'' with the ''m''-fold tensor product of '''Q'''<sub>''p''</sub>(1). Denoting by '''Q'''<sub>''p''</sub>(&minus;1) the [[dual representation]] of '''Q'''<sub>''p''</sub>(1), the ''−m''th Tate twist of ''V'' can be defined as

:<math>V\otimes\mathbf{Q}_p(-1)^{\otimes m}.</math>
